family.tagline: Sourdough upstairs, a baby downstairs, orders on the Core.
family.story: Eleni bakes sourdough for weekend pre-orders in the big upstairs kitchen. Marcus works from home in logistics and keeps the order table in line. Their baby, Ari, sleeps one flight down.

companion.name: Iris
companion.job: Drafts the weekly pre-order menu and customer notes from what Eleni texts it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Eleni sends the menu.

companion.name: Walt
companion.job: Opens NocoDB in its own browser and updates the weekend order table.
companion.limits: Updates rows Marcus names. He checks the table.

popup.title: A parcel, one flight up
popup.body: The parcel lands at the garden-floor door. Marcus carries it through the family room and the dining room, then up the stair to the kitchen.

popup.title: Four things in the parcel
popup.body: Eleni lays out the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Its footprint is about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Marcus plugs in the cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it while the loaf proofs
popup.body: While a loaf proofs, Eleni joins the Core's own network from her phone. Then she picks the home network.

popup.title: Pick your first agents and apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Marcus picks Hermes for Eleni and OpenClaw for himself. He adds NocoDB, KitchenOwl, Akaunting and Listmonk, then they walk away.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Iris says good morning
popup.body: Eleni texts the agent she named Iris. Iris answers, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: eleni
say.text: Good morning, Eleni. Iris here. What are we baking?

beats.capability: a shared grocery list, recipe book, meal planner and expense tracker for the household

popup.title: Index cards become a recipe book
popup.body: Eleni types her first stained sourdough card into KitchenOwl at the island, and the recipe book begins.

beats.capability: a spreadsheet-database with real Python formulas, stored as a SQLite file you can copy

popup.title: Dough math that recalculates
popup.body: Eleni keeps her baker's percentages in a Grist table. Change the loaf count, and the flour and water weights recalculate.

beats.capability: write a wiki or a set of manuals in books, chapters and pages, with search and history

popup.title: The starter handbook, written down
popup.body: Eleni writes the starter handbook in BookStack: how to feed it, when to shape, which shelf runs hot. A Saturday helper can read it at the counter.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Iris drafts the weekend menu
popup.body: Eleni texts Iris this weekend's loaves. Iris drafts the menu note. Eleni sends it from Listmonk herself.

say.speaker: eleni
say.text: Draft ready. Please read it before you send it.

beats.capability: turn a database into a spreadsheet-style app without writing code

popup.title: Walt keeps the order table
popup.body: Marcus tells Walt which sourdough customers confirmed. Walt opens NocoDB in its own browser and updates the order table. Marcus checks every row.

beats.capability: invoicing, expenses, customers and profit and loss for a small business

popup.title: The bakehouse books, at the table
popup.body: Eleni enters the week's flour bills and pre-order takings in Akaunting. The bakehouse's expenses and profit and loss stay on the Core.

beats.capability: merge, split, compress and convert PDFs on your own Core

popup.title: Pickup sheets, merged into one
popup.body: Marcus merges the weekend pickup sheets into one PDF with Stirling-PDF. The merging runs on the Core, and he prints a single file.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: A regular asks for a swap
popup.body: A regular wants rye in place of her usual loaf. Eleni texts Iris from the couch. Iris drafts a reply, and Eleni sends it.

beats.capability: store every password in a vault you host

popup.title: Supplier logins, kept in a vault
popup.body: Marcus moves the supplier logins into VaultWarden by the fireplace. The vault runs on the Core and works with the Bitwarden apps.

beats.capability: a small CalDAV and CardDAV server for your calendars and contacts

popup.title: One pickup calendar, two phones
popup.body: Marcus sets up Baikal at the writing desk. Eleni's phone and his read the same pickup calendar, so both see the same Saturday slots.

beats.capability: a local video recorder with object detection for your IP cameras

popup.title: The pickup door, recorded at home
popup.body: Customers collect their loaves at the garden-floor door. Marcus points the family's IP camera at it. Frigate records the doorway, and the video stays on the Core.

beats.capability: turn a folder of photos and videos into a private feed with albums and a timeline

popup.title: Loaf photos on the TV
popup.body: Saturday's loaves are sold. Marcus opens Foldergram on the TV, and the week's loaf photos scroll by as a private feed with a timeline.

beats.capability: assign and track household chores and recurring tasks

popup.title: A chore wheel for two
popup.body: Eleni and Marcus assign the laundry, the dishes and the flour run in Donetick. Recurring chores come back on schedule.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos on your own Core

popup.title: Ari's first months, kept at home
popup.body: Marcus adds the week's photos of Ari to Immich. The family library sits on the Core, backed up and searchable.

beats.capability: listen to your audiobooks and podcasts, and pick up where you left off on any device

popup.title: A quiet audiobook for night feeds
popup.body: During the night feed, Eleni plays an audiobook in Audiobookshelf, turned low. It remembers her place, so the next night starts where this one ended.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: Rosemary for the focaccia
popup.body: Eleni logs the rosemary and thyme for the focaccia in HortusFox, and the care history stays on the Core.

beats.capability: plan, map and share hiking and biking routes from GPX files

popup.title: A slow walk, mapped at home
popup.body: On Sunday, Marcus plans a stroller route along the water in Wanderer. He loads a GPX file, and the saved route lives on the Core.

popup.title: One flight up, one Core
popup.body: Sourdough upstairs, a baby downstairs. The Papadakis-Roy family runs it all from one Companion Core.

closing.body: Your sourdough, your orders and your evenings can live on a Companion Core at home. Start with one recipe card in KitchenOwl.

notes: Owner sign-off open: the FTUE hotspot flow is written as the owner specified and is not on the fact sheet (STORY-BIBLE section 15, item 1).

Cast suggested Mealie for the recipe cards. Mealie has no QA screenshot and reviewed.json is empty, so KitchenOwl (recipe book, screenshot QA) carries the story. Swap in one line if the owner reviews Mealie.
Cottage-food rules differ by place: the story says nothing about licences, permits or food regulations, as the care note asks.
Listmonk needs an SMTP provider to send at volume (catalog caveat). The story only says Eleni writes and sends the note herself, with no delivery claim.

floor-camera: Frigate on the pickup door records customers collecting loaves. Check that the owner is comfortable with a camera on a door that customers use. No "prevents" or viewing-away claim is made.
water-walk: Wanderer plans routes from a GPX file; map tiles may come from outside the house. The text claims only that the saved route lives on the Core.
Upstairs Bakehouse is not named in the text; the casting business name is invented. Voice-over lexicon: Papadakis, Eleni, Iris, Walt, Grist, Foldergram, Wanderer, Donetick, Listmonk.
Town Spindle Cove and street Ledgewater Street are invented; still needs the human map check.
